title: A volcano helped give us Frankenstein

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1815, a volcano helped give us Frankenstein.
beats.visual: Volcano erupts; its ash cloud morphs into a stitched monster silhouette

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: April 1815: Mount Tambora erupts in today's Indonesia.
beats.visual: Sketch map of Indonesia, pin on Sumbawa; NASA PD photo of Tambora's crater

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: How does a volcano write books?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Through the weather. Its haze cooled the planet. But there was a problem.
beats.visual: Grey haze spreads across a globe; thermometer drops

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Exactly. 1816 became the year without a summer. Snow fell in New England in June, and crops failed.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Lake Geneva, June 1816. Rain trapped Byron, Mary Shelley and friends in Villa Diodati. Byron proposed a ghost-story contest.
beats.visual: PD photo of Villa Diodati with rain; PD Byron portrait slides in; candle and paper

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Mary began Frankenstein, published in 1818. Polidori wrote The Vampyre.
beats.visual: PD page of Mary Shelley's Frankenstein draft; PD Rothwell portrait of Mary Shelley slides in

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: None of them knew a volcano made the rain. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Rain turns to ash flakes; History Sketches corner logo

description: Mount Tambora's 1815 eruption cooled the planet and made 1816 the year without a summer. Trapped indoors by rain at Villa Diodati, Byron proposed a ghost-story contest, and Mary Shelley began Frankenstein. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #frankenstein #volcano
